recreation_brief:
1. Set the full-slide background to light gray #E8E8E8.
2. Draw the red frame: a thin red (#CC0000) rectangle outline inset ~3% from all four slide edges (within the ~2%-6% inset range), plus a horizontal red (#CC0000) rule at ~29% height spanning the frame width; keep the title band above the rule light gray and fill the content panel below the rule with white #FFFFFF.
3. Place the title: bold red (#CC0000) sans-serif, ~40pt, centered in the title band (~5%-28% height), exact text 'What would a k-D filter looks like?' (keep the source grammar verbatim).
4. Place the handwritten caption: black marker/handwritten-style font (Comic Sans-like), ~24pt, exact text 'e.g. Sobel 2-D filter', at ~10% width / ~35% height (top of the left content region).
5. Insert the Grumpy Cat meme photo (white cat frowning on a gray/white pillow; white Impact-style all-caps captions with black outline: 'I LOVE MATH' at top, 'IT MAKES PEOPLE CRY!' at bottom) at ~8%-45% width / ~45%-85% height.
6. Overlay the Sobel matrix on that photo: very large red (#CC0000) digits (~36pt) in three rows '-1  0  1' / '-2  0  2' / '-1  0  1', centered on the photo, with two oversized red square brackets (left and right) spanning all three rows; the 0 column sits roughly over the cat's face.
7. Build the color-channel stack at ~45%-75% width / ~38%-85% height: three overlapping copies of the same meme photo, each tinted one solid color — red #B00000 copy at the back (top-right), green #00A651 copy in the middle, blue #0000CC copy at the front (largest, shifted left and down) — overlapping so all three top edges stay visible.
8. Place the label '3-D Filter': bold red (#CC0000) sans-serif, ~20pt, at ~76%-90% width / ~40%-46% height (top-right of the content panel).
9. Draw the cube diagram at ~73%-93% width / ~50%-85% height: an isometric 3x3x3 cube (PowerPoint 'Cube' shape or a 3x3 grid of small squares on each of the three visible faces) with light gray #D9D9D9 faces, black grid lines, and one black digit per visible cell — top face rows: 2, 3, [?] / 4, 6, 9 / 7, 8, 9; front-left face rows: 9, 7, 1 / 5, 1, 3 / 5, 3, 6; front-right face rows: 3, 9, 5 / 1, 5, 4 / 6, 2, 4; keep [?] as an unreadable placeholder and do not guess a digit.
10. Place the 'Third D' annotation at the cube's lower-left: small bold yellow (#FFD700) text with black outline reading 'Third D', plus two short black arrows forming a double-headed dimension indicator pointing along the cube's receding depth axis.
11. Optional video chrome only (not slide content): a black bar across the full bottom width (~92%-100% height) with a small solid red (#CC0000) rectangle at its left end — include only if the video-frame look must be replicated.
